changes: p2 Somara: removed residence 'Gauḍadeśa'. That belongs to the author Raghunātha, not the scribe.
p2 Somara: still scribe, low confidence. Read the vernacular note as 'pustaka pūraṇa bhaye … Somara dekhyā, Somara likhyā'.
date.month normalized to 'Āṣāḍha (dvitīya, i.e. second/intercalary)'. Paksa normalized to 'kṛṣṇa (vadi)' and tithi to '13 (trayodaśī)'.
Notes: confirmed that ŚS 1700 and VS 1835 agree (both 1778 CE). Added the reading of the vernacular note.

notes:
The colophon gives two dates, Śaka 1700 and Vikrama Saṃvat 1835. They agree: both are 1778 CE, and the catalogue fields match. 'dutīā āṣānha' probably means the second Āṣāḍha, which would make it an intercalary month. This has not been checked against an ephemeris.

The closing note is vernacular and corrupt: †ke prasataka puraṇa bhaye ena somaradeṣyā somaralīṣyā†. A likely reading is '[yah] pustaka pūraṇa bhaye; Somara dekhyā, Somara likhyā' ('the book was completed; Somara saw/checked it, Somara wrote it'). On that reading Somara is the scribe, and possibly also the checker of the copy. The name may also be Somāru, or the text may be a garbled 'somavāra' (Monday), so confidence is low.

'Gauḍadeśīya' describes the author Raghunātha Sārvabhauma, not the scribe.
